name: crypto_random_bytes
description: Generates cryptographically secure random bytes using OpenSSL's RAND_bytes(). Length must be between 1 and 4,294,967,295 bytes. Each call produces different random bytes.

examples.code: SELECT crypto_random_bytes(16);
SELECT crypto_random_bytes(32);

name: crypto_hash_agg
description: Computes a cryptographic hash over multiple rows using the specified algorithm. ORDER BY is required to ensure deterministic results. Returns the same hash as crypto_hash() would for an equivalent ordered list. Returns NULL for empty result sets.

examples.code: SELECT crypto_hash_agg('sha2-256', column_name ORDER BY id);
SELECT crypto_hash_agg('blake3', data ORDER BY timestamp);

name: crypto_hmac
description: Computes an HMAC (Hash-based Message Authentication Code) of the message using the specified algorithm and key. Supports all hash algorithms except blake3, which requires exactly 32 bytes for the key.

examples.code: SELECT crypto_hmac('sha2-256', 'secret_key', 'message to authenticate');

name: crypto_hash
description: Computes a cryptographic hash of the input value using the specified algorithm. Supported algorithms: blake3, sha2-256, sha2-512, sha3-256, sha3-512, md5, sha1, and more. Accepts strings, integers, floats, dates, timestamps, UUIDs, and lists of fixed-length types.

examples.code: SELECT crypto_hash('sha2-256', 'hello world');
SELECT crypto_hash('blake3', 42);
SELECT crypto_hash('sha2-256', [1, 2, 3]);
